detail: The fix for `internal-command-reachable` scanned shell and Python harnesses for the dead top-level spelling, but its globs never matched a `.ps1` file and its regex only recognised a command sitting next to the word `reproit`. The Windows harness spells it neither way: the binary is a variable and the command is a standalone argument string, `$start.Arguments = "__uia"`. So `windows-uia`, the release gate all three Windows targets own, exited 2 before the runner started and has been red since d957df5, which is why the retained Windows evidence names an older commit. Running the gate on the native x86_64 Windows guest at 414c1a14 is what surfaced it. The defect lives in CI harness wiring, so no runtime guard can hold it; the bounded regression test now also scans PowerShell harnesses and rejects a whole quoted argument that is exactly one internal command, failing on the parent (it cites the Windows harness line) and passing on the fix.
